assets.prompt: Overhead handheld smartphone photograph, shot at a slight angle so the sheet keystones a little, of a large sheet of pale cream gridded drafting paper lying on a wooden table under a window with soft daylight falling across it. Hand-drawn across the sheet in one deep blue-black ink are the founder's own letterforms: the numerals 0 to 9 PLUS an extra fourth glyph so there are ELEVEN numeral forms in total, an open-top 4 (the diagonal and stem left open at the top) drawn right beside a closed-top 4 (a fully closed triangular counter), with nothing marking which is preferred. Below and around the numerals the full alphabet A to Z is hand-drawn. The glyphs are drawn at noticeably DIFFERENT SIZES and scattered as separate, disjoint pen strokes with clear gaps between them, not joined into any single mark. The TOP TWO ROWS are drawn with a visibly HEAVIER, thicker, darker nib than everything below, but because each glyph is a different size this heavier weight is not obvious at a glance. Across the LOWER THIRD of the sheet the pen pressure is much lighter, so the ink there is faint and pale and sits close in tonal value to the printed pale-grey grid lines, the drawn line and the printed grid nearly merging. The rounder glyphs (0, 6, 8, 9, O, Q, and the closed 4) have small, tight interior counters. Realistic drafting paper with a faint printed grid, soft window light, casual real-world snapshot, not a scan, no colour except the single ink, no logos.

assets.prompt: Handheld smartphone photograph, shot slightly from above, of an old running singlet in a faded mid-tone heather grey-blue athletic knit laid out flat on a table, with a single soft fold running diagonally across the LOWER LEFT of the garment. Screen-printed on the chest in ONE deep navy ink is a compound club lockup: a ring of small-capital type reading IRONWAY RUN CLUB / PROVIDENCE / EST 1994 arranged in a circle, a thin outer arc line just inside the type ring, and at the centre a separate geometric device of a chevron sitting above a short horizontal rail line. The print is a few seasons old and slightly faded. The athletic KNIT TEXTURE breaks the printed edges into a fine sawtooth so the letter and device edges are ragged at the fibre level rather than smooth. Along the shadowed diagonal fold across the lower left, the navy ink and the heather jersey fall close together in tonal value so the print nearly disappears into the fabric there. One ink only, no other colours, realistic worn cotton-blend jersey with subtle pilling, soft uneven daylight, casual real-world snapshot, not a studio shot, no photographic brand logos.

assets.content:
LAYOUT SPEC for last season's Founders Five race bib, the printer's returned press PDF (flat, single record; to be reverse-engineered downstream into a live merge template).

Document: single bib, 152 x 203 mm PORTRAIT (6 x 8 in), NO bleed box present (trim = media box, 0 mm bleed), fonts embedded, ONE ink only, Rail Navy #1F2A44 on a Bib White #F4F2EC ground. This is the file the club's printer already ran last spring.

WHAT IT LOOKS LIKE PRINTED (four apparent blocks, top to bottom):
- HEAD: the club mark, centred at the top, about 34 mm tall.
- BIG NUMBER: the runner's assigned number, very large (about 90 mm cap height), centred in the middle third, the thing a marshal reads across a wet road.
- NAME: the member's name in a bold condensed sans, one line, directly under the number.
- DETAILS: a small two-line block at the foot, pace group on one line and emergency contact name plus phone on the next.

HOW IT IS ACTUALLY SET (the reverse-engineering trap):
- The club mark at the HEAD is a PLACED RASTER IMAGE (a flattened low-res scan of the mark) sitting in one rectangular graphic frame. It is last season's placed scan, not live artwork, so the recovered mark plate must replace it rather than sit beside it.
- The BIG NUMBER is its own single text frame.
- The NAME, the PACE GROUP and the EMERGENCY CONTACT are NOT three addressable frames. They are ONE continuous threaded text story in a SINGLE text frame that runs name -> pace group -> emergency contact top to bottom, separated only by line breaks. So the four blocks the eye reads map to just one image frame + one number frame + one continuous story frame, and there is no separate frame to bind pace group or emergency contact into.
- The NAME sits at the head of that story in a FIXED MEASURE, a fixed column width sized to last season's longest name (about 22 characters). Text longer than the measure does not push the layout, does not wrap to a second line and raises no overset warning in the output. It simply stops, so a member whose name is longer than the measure loses the tail of their surname silently.
- The readout a conversion gives of that story is lossy: it can report the story with one run dropped (for example the pace-group line) while keeping its line break, so every field position after the omission is short by one run. A per-frame mapping computed from that description is wrong, and the validator still returns valid with no warnings.

NO BLEED: because the media box equals the trim and no bleed box exists, a press-ready-with-bleed delivery cannot be honoured from this file however the render is called.

FIELD LABELS the downstream mapping must resolve (present as content, not as visible tokens): MEMBER_NAME | ASSIGNED_NUMBER | PACE_GROUP | EMERGENCY_CONTACT | EMERGENCY_PHONE, plus the MARK image at the head.

Colours: Bib White #F4F2EC ground, Rail Navy #1F2A44 ink (the number, the name, the details and the placed mark all reproduce in the one ink).

assets.content:
IRONWAY RUN CLUB — heat transfer shop notes (Providence Print & Press)

Hi folks, here is what we need on our end to cut and press your numbers on the new kit. One colour only, same as always. We cut it out of a single sheet of transfer film, so there are no shades and no outlines, just the one flat shape. The colour you picked off our rack is our stock Marshal Orange film; it is the only orange we keep, so the artwork has to work in that one flat colour sitting on your navy singlet.

BACK PANEL PRINT AREA (usable area, per singlet size):
- S: 9 in wide x 11 in tall
- M: 10 in wide x 12 in tall
- L: 11 in wide x 13 in tall
- XL: 12 in wide x 14 in tall
Keep everything inside that box. We cannot press right up to a seam.

NUMBER HEIGHT: you have always run an 8 inch tall number and it reads well from the far side of the road, so keep it at 8 inches unless you tell us otherwise. Any club letters that sit on the number line should be capped to that same 8 inch height.

MINIMUM STROKE: our cutter cannot hold a line thinner than 3 mm (about 1/8 inch) at final pressed size. Anything thinner than that lifts at the edge in the first wash and peels by June. If any part of the lettering comes in under 3 mm at 8 inch height, put it in your note and we will thicken it, or you will lose it on the press.

We press at 305 F for 15 seconds, so the film has to be one clean single shape with no tiny islands or closed-up holes. Send us one flat cut colour and we are good to go.

— Providence Print & Press
